visualize.boxplot_how_to_read_title: ⓘ How to read a box plot
visualize.boxplot_how_to_read_content: A box plot summarizes how values are distributed. The box contains the middle 50% of values: the left edge is Q1 (25% of values are lower), the right edge is Q3 (75% of values are lower). The thick line inside the box is the median. The two whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values excluding outliers. Points outside are outliers: values more than 1.5 times the box width (IQR) away from the box. A narrower box indicates values are closer together; an off-center median indicates skewed data.

visualize.corr_method_tooltip: Spearman is suitable for rating scales and ordinal data; Pearson for continuous numbers. Auto-selected based on your data.
visualize.corr_grid_caption_tooltip: Each cell is the number of respondents who chose that level combination. Darker cells = more respondents.
visualize.corr_what_is_r_content: r (correlation coefficient) indicates whether the answers to two questions tend to change together. r ranges from −1 to 1. Near 1: respondents who chose high levels for one usually chose high for the other. Near −1: respondents who chose high for one tended to choose low for the other. Near 0: little to no relationship. Strength: under 0.3 weak · 0.3–0.5 moderate · 0.5–0.7 fairly strong · 0.7 and above strong. n is the number of respondents who answered both questions. Correlation does not imply causation.
visualize.corr_threshold_tooltip: Only list pairs with correlation magnitude r at or above this level. The list always ranks the strongest pairs first, so changing the threshold mainly alters the number of pairs shown.
visualize.corr_strength_tooltip: Strength based on the magnitude of r: under 0.3 weak, 0.3–0.5 moderate, 0.5–0.7 fairly strong, from 0.7 strong.
visualize.corr_direction_tooltip: Positive: both variables increase or decrease together. Negative: one increases while the other decreases.
visualize.corr_n_tooltip: Number of respondents who answered both questions. Larger n yields more reliable results.
visualize.corr_discrete_positive: Respondents who chose high levels in [{{colA}}] also tended to choose high levels in [{{colB}}].
visualize.corr_discrete_negative: Respondents who chose high levels in [{{colA}}] tended to choose low levels in [{{colB}}].
visualize.corr_continuous_positive: Those with high values in [{{colA}}] also tended to have high values in [{{colB}}].
